subject: Clarify discrete billing steps and rounding/floor policy for blended contexts
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@finpay.com>, FinPay Procurement <procurement@finpay.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-09-09T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Billing question — discrete step rounding for blended call patterns

Hi Maria / FinPay procurement team,

Thanks again for the walk-through yesterday. After reviewing the sample invoice you sent, I noticed a few line items where the token math shows fractional units and the invoice appears to have been rounded in different places (some lines rounded up, some rounded to nearest). To avoid surprises on future invoices, could you confirm which of these scenarios matter most to you?

Quick summary of our questions so we can give a single, clear rule:
- When a single API request contains both a short prompt and a long streaming response (hybrid call), do we bill the request as a single "metering event" and apply rounding once, or do we split prompt/response into separate metering events and apply rounding to each?
- If we apply rounding per metering event, what quantum should we use (our default is a 1-token quantum for hosted calls; we also support 100-token quanta for some enterprise SKUs)?
- For invoices where small microbursts account for <1% of monthly tokens, would FinPay prefer us to aggregate and show a single smoothing line vs. itemized rounding on each call?

I'm attaching our most recent pricing summary (pricing_summary_v2.pdf) and can include an example CSV if you want. Proposed next step: short call with Jordan (sales ops) and Tessa (pricing) so we can lock down the exact reconciliation text we put in the contract and invoice examples. Are you available Tue/Wed next week for a 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: pricing_summary_v2.pdf

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@finpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing question — discrete step rounding for blended call patterns

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the clear list — really helpful. Attaching a short CSV that shows three invoice lines from our last bill with the token math and how we expected rounding to be presented (example-invoice.csv).

What matters most for us:
- Predictability for finance: our auditors want a deterministic rule we can encode (e.g., "round up to the next quantum per metering event").
- Simplicity on the invoice: we prefer a single smoothing/adjustment line rather than dozens of tiny rounded items, especially for microbursts under a small threshold.

Questions: what do you mean by "metering event" in the host vs. enterprise SKU sense? Also, will any smoothing credits be applied automatically or only via manually-approved concession?

We can do Wed 2028-09-13 10:00am PT or Thu 2028-09-14 9:00am PT for a 30-min call — whichever works for your team.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Cloud Ops, FinPay
maria.gonzalez@finpay.com

Attachments: example-invoice.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Billing question — discrete step rounding for blended call patterns

Jordan / Tessa — forwarding FinPay's note and attached sample invoice. They want a deterministic rule auditors can rely on and prefer an invoice-level smoothing line for tiny microbursts. Below I've drafted a short, customer-facing reconciliation paragraph we can send back — please edit: 

DRAFT wording (please confirm):
"Redwood bills tokens using discrete metering events. For Hosted API customers, a metering event is defined as a single API request; for Dedicated/Private SKUs the metering event may be the session or batch depending on your configured aggregation policy. Token usage is totaled per metering event and then rounded up to the billing quantum associated with your SKU (default quantum: Hosted = 1 token, Dedicated = 100 tokens). After per-event rounding, Redwood will aggregate usage across the billing period. For customers with consistent microburst noise below 2% of monthly usage, Redwood can optionally apply a smoothing adjustment to reduce invoice itemization; smoothing credits are applied as a one-line invoice adjustment and must be agreed before the billing period."

Notes / asks for you both:
- Jordan: is the 2% smoothing threshold reasonable? If not, propose alternative (we've offered 1–3% in prior pilots). Also confirm whether our internal billing system can apply smoothing automatically for pilot customers vs. manual credits only.
- Tessa: if we make smoothing an "opt-in with 12-month commit" concession, what discount / credit budget should sales expect? FinPay is mid-size and may push for a one-off smoothing credit for their onboarding month.

I'll wait for your edits — Maria is available Wed 9/13 10am PT which would be tight but doable if we lock this today.

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-13T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing question — discrete step rounding for blended call patterns

Kimberly / Tessa — quick take and recommended customer language below. I ran this by Finance and Billing Ops.

Policy (concise, to share with customer):
1) Definition: "Metering event" = one API request for Hosted API customers; for Dedicated and Private deployments, the metering event follows the configured aggregation policy (per-request or per-session) as documented in your deployment agreement.
2) Rounding: We apply rounding at the metering-event level and always round up to the configured billing quantum for that SKU. Hosted default quantum = 1 token; enterprise/Dedicated configurable quanta = 50 or 100 tokens (set per contract).
3) Aggregation & invoice presentation: Per-event rounded usage is summed across the invoice. For customers who opt into smoothing, Billing Ops will add a single adjustment line labeled "Microburst smoothing credit" that reduces invoice itemization.
4) Smoothing rules & concessions: Billing Ops can apply smoothing automatically for pilots if pre-authorized by Sales Ops. Our recommended pilot concession: one-time invoice smoothing credit equal to the sum of per-event rounding deltas capped at 3% of the first month’s invoice, subject to a 12-month commit.

Answers to your asks:
- 2% vs 3% threshold: Finance prefers the 3% cap for pilot concessions (gives us headroom); we can offer 3% for FinPay's onboarding month and revert to 1–2% thereafter if they request ongoing smoothing.
- Automation vs manual: Billing Ops can automate the smoothing credit for pilot customers if Sales Ops flags the HubSpot deal ID (FP-2028-09-BLEND-3). Otherwise credits are manual.

Suggested reply to FinPay (short):
"Thanks Maria — to be fully deterministic: Redwood rounds up per metering event to the billing quantum for your SKU (Hosted default 1 token; enterprise/Dedicated configurable to 50/100). For the onboarding month we can apply a one-time smoothing credit capped at 3% of that invoice if you agree to a 12‑month commit; after that we can discuss whether to keep smoothing as an ongoing opt-in. Can we confirm Wed 9/13 10am PT for a 30-min sync?"

If that looks good I can send the reply and include the HubSpot link to flag Billing Ops. Tessa — if you want to tighten the concession (2% cap instead of 3%), say so and I'll update the text.

-Jordan
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
